angle: Voice feedback only pays off if you redesign the intake-to-resolution pipeline, not just add a new inbox.
sourceTitle: Whispering Complaints Into Your Phone May Be the Future of Customer Feedback
linkedinPost:
Customers don’t want another survey—they want to be heard.

A WIRED piece profiles “voice-note” feedback tools that let customers record complaints instead of filling forms. Lower friction means more (and richer) signal: tone, urgency, specifics you never get from star ratings.

My take from the front lines: this only drives value if you rewire what happens after the note arrives. The win isn’t collecting audio. It’s turning those minutes into resolved issues and product changes.

What works in enterprises:
- Auto-transcribe and summarize for agents, including sentiment and urgency.
- Route to the right team with clear SLAs, not a generic queue.
- Close the loop: notify customers when their issue is fixed, and tag the fix.

Measure outcomes, not uploads: time-to-first-response, first-contact resolution, dollar impact of defect reductions, and topics that trigger churn.

Two cautions: get consent and retention right (privacy), and support multilingual/accents without bias—otherwise your richest signals come from the easiest voices to parse.

If you’re piloting voice feedback, do you have a “capture → route → resolve → learn” map on one page? #CustomerExperience #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI
